answers.explanation: Dynamo, Cassandra, and Riak work this way.
Version numbers tell the client which copy is newest.
Three of five must answer each operation.
Every write needs all three replicas.
1 + 1 is not greater than 3, so the sets may not overlap.
Anti-entropy is the background process that compares replicas.
With sloppy quorums, the overlap no longer holds.
Sloppy quorums, concurrent writes, and partial failures all break the guarantee.
